nodes.label: Web Push Notifications Spec
nodes.rationale: This iteration is deliberately scoped to plumbing only — subscription lifecycle, storage, and delivery; actual notification triggers (MQTT-driven, scheduled) and preference-filtering UI are explicitly out of scope and deferred to a later slice.

nodes.label: cameraOrderStorage Adapter
nodes.rationale: Per-user server-side storage is explicitly deferred; the storage adapter interface (loadOrder/saveOrder) allows swapping localStorage for a server-backed implementation later without changing callers.

nodes.label: iOS Native Pull-to-Refresh Conflict
nodes.rationale: iOS Safari's native pull-to-refresh performs a full page reload and competes with any custom gesture; overscroll-behavior-y:contain does not suppress it on iOS, so the reliable cross-platform fix is intercepting touchmove and calling preventDefault() while the custom gesture is active.

nodes.label: Edit Mode Interaction Pattern
nodes.rationale: An explicit Edit mode resolves the conflict between vertical drag gestures and the existing pull-to-refresh interaction; pull-to-refresh is disabled only while editing.

nodes.label: clearFrigateCache Function
nodes.rationale: The entire cache is cleared rather than selectively invalidated because the cache is small and TTL-bounded; selective invalidation was explicitly out of scope.

nodes.label: parseFrigateEvent Function
nodes.rationale: Only type:'new' events trigger notifications, preventing repeat notifications as the same event later updates or ends; malformed payloads must not throw and return null instead.

nodes.label: clearCache Server Function
nodes.rationale: A dedicated server function is used instead of a ?bustCache query param because the cache is server-side in-memory and the client cannot bypass it directly; this separates the 'clear cache' intent from the 'load data' intent and avoids URL pollution.

nodes.label: MQTT-Driven Push Notifications with Per-Camera Opt-Out Spec
nodes.rationale: Connects existing push infrastructure to MQTT so users get real-time notifications, batching per-camera bursts into a single notification to reduce spam.

nodes.label: Opt-Out Default Preference Model
nodes.rationale: All cameras default to enabled (opt-out model) so zero setup is required when a new camera is added to Frigate.

nodes.label: Per-Camera 10-Second Batching Window
nodes.rationale: Per-camera windows are used because users can opt out of individual cameras and cross-camera bundling would complicate filtering; an in-memory Map + setTimeout is sufficient since no persistence is needed — worst case on restart is one unbatched notification.

nodes.label: EventBatcher Burst Detection
nodes.rationale: Current behavior: EventBatcher flushes a camera's first event immediately (leading edge), batches follow-ups into EVENT_BATCH_WINDOW_MS windows, and each flush reports whether it opens a new activity burst (no events for EVENT_BURST_GAP_MS) or continues one — bursts alert once and continuations silently patch the existing notification, paced for Apple endpoints via APPLE_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS.

nodes.label: Feature-Sliced Architecture
nodes.rationale: Each feature owns its own folder under src/features/ with all of its components, hooks, utilities, types, and server logic; features must never import from each other, and shared logic goes in src/features/shared/ — duplication is preferred over cross-feature coupling.

nodes.label: Long-Term Memory Vault (Obsidian docs/memory)
nodes.rationale: bd (beads) is for actionable, short-lived issue tracking; the Obsidian vault at docs/memory/ is for durable, explanatory knowledge (architectural rationale, platform gotchas, decision records) so it isn't lost at session end — the two stores are deliberately kept separate.

nodes.label: Opus-Plans/Sonnet-Implements Delegation
nodes.rationale: Opus is reserved for planning (understanding the codebase, designing approach, decomposing work, reviewing diffs, architectural/security trade-offs) so the expensive reasoning model is not spent on mechanical work; Sonnet implements pre-decomposed, Sonnet-sized chunks with concrete file targets and no open design questions left unresolved.

nodes.label: No AI Attribution Rule
nodes.rationale: No Co-Authored-By trailers, 'Generated with Claude' footers, or other AI attribution may appear in commit messages, PR titles/bodies, code comments, or any pushed artifact, for any AI tool.

nodes.label: Mandatory Session Completion Workflow
nodes.rationale: Work is not considered complete until git push succeeds; the mandated workflow (file issues, run quality gates, update issue status, push, clean up, verify) exists so work is never left stranded only on the local machine.

nodes.label: Isomorphic-by-Default Boundary Problem
nodes.rationale: All TanStack Start code is isomorphic by default; a server-only helper imported into a shared module can be tree-shaken into the client bundle, crashing the app or silently exposing secrets — hence explicit server/client boundary primitives and file-naming conventions are required.

nodes.label: Horizontal Slicing Anti-Pattern
nodes.rationale: Writing all tests first and then all implementation ('horizontal slicing') produces tests that check imagined behavior/shape rather than actual behavior, making them insensitive to real regressions.

nodes.label: Red-Green-Refactor Cycle
nodes.rationale: Enforces strict RED-GREEN-REFACTOR with hard gates because LLMs are especially prone to skipping tests or writing them after implementation, which produces code that looks tested but was never actually validated.

nodes.label: Vertical Slicing / Tracer Bullet
nodes.rationale: One test then one implementation, repeated: the first vertical slice is a tracer bullet proving the path works end-to-end before investing in breadth, so a bad design assumption costs one wasted cycle instead of five.

nodes.label: Traefik CSP unsafe-inline Header
nodes.rationale: The CSP's script-src must allow 'unsafe-inline' because TanStack Start's streaming SSR emits dynamic per-request inline scripts (hydration bootstrap + $tsr stream barrier) that cannot be pre-hashed; a hash/nonce would make browsers ignore 'unsafe-inline' and break hydration.

nodes.label: Loopback Port Binding (Traefik Bypass Prevention)
nodes.rationale: The production app's port is bound to 127.0.0.1 only, not 0.0.0.0, so Traefik reaches it over the internal 'proxy' network — this keeps the app off a plain-HTTP path that would bypass Traefik's TLS termination and security headers.

nodes.label: isValidCameraName / isValidEventId Validators
nodes.rationale: User-supplied camera names and event IDs are forwarded into Frigate backend URL paths; validating them before use prevents SSRF and path traversal against the Frigate backend.

nodes.label: requireSession()
nodes.rationale: TanStack Start createServerFn endpoints are directly callable via HTTP at /_serverFn/{hash}; route-level layout guards only protect client-side navigation, so every handler touching protected data must call requireSession() itself as its first operation rather than relying on route hierarchy.

nodes.label: EventBatcher (fixed-window description)
nodes.rationale: Describes EventBatcher as simply accumulating events per camera and flushing after a fixed EVENT_BATCH_WINDOW_MS window; it does not mention the leading-edge flush or burst-detection logic present in the current CLAUDE.md description, suggesting this doc has gone stale relative to the implementation.

nodes.label: Runtime-Portable SQLite Driver (openSqlite)
nodes.rationale: openSqlite() branches at runtime between better-sqlite3 (Node, used by Vitest) and bun:sqlite (Bun, production) behind one shared interface; a Node dev process and a Bun production server must never run concurrently against the same DB file because WAL/SHM file ownership differs between the two drivers.

nodes.label: Bun-Only Package Manager Enforcement
nodes.rationale: package.json's preinstall script (npx only-allow bun) aborts npm/pnpm/yarn installs; CI (oven-sh/setup-bun), the Dockerfile (oven/bun), and all scripts standardize on Bun so build and runtime behavior stay consistent.

nodes.label: URL Field Forward Compatibility
nodes.rationale: The push payload always includes a url field so future notification types (e.g. /camera-events/{id}) can be added without changing the service-worker handler.

nodes.label: withRouter Storybook Decorator
nodes.rationale: A minimal createRouter + createMemoryHistory setup is sufficient because stories never navigate; only the router context requirement needs satisfying for components using Link or useRouteContext.
